title: The Southern Inheritance That Walked Back

features.name: returning root
features.desc-on-touch: Roots emerge from earth and remember their own beginnings. What was taken walks back on its own schedule.

features.name: property markers dissolving
features.desc-on-touch: Fences you search for cannot be found. The land walks through ownership like a body through a room.

features.name: inheritance made living
features.desc-on-touch: You hold something that belonged to someone before you. Here it is held by the tree that never stopped growing.

features.name: canopy teaching
features.desc-on-touch: The crown of the forest whispers back to itself. It has learned how to pass on what it knows without words.

features.name: ground memory
features.desc-on-touch: Soil that remembers every foot that crossed it. Ownership could not compete with roots, and the roots remember.

inscription: the property line became a place the forest could walk through; inheritance is not owned, it returns because the roots remember it was always leaving

reverie.title: REVERIE — walking the property line until it stopped matteri
narr: You walk beside Katita through a forest that was never fully yours.
She stops at a tree marked with a faded survey line. 'It knew this was her
before the line was drawn,' she says. 'The roots remember.'
You stand there while the light falls. The fence was never a place.
It was just a line the trees grew through anyway.
